prompt: Let $R\subseteq A\times A$, with all quantified variables ranging over $A$. Which property is defined exactly by $\forall x\forall y\; (x\ne y\Rightarrow (R(x,y)\lor R(y,x)))$?

answers.explanation: Every pair of distinct elements is comparable in at least one direction. This convention imposes no condition on loops.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Mutual relatedness forces equality. Self-loops are allowed. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every ordered pair is present, including every loop. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
Every pair is comparable, including an element with itself, so all loops are required. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
An element has at most one outgoing related element; it need not have any. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
One related pair suffices; the other elements may be isolated. That is a different condition from the displayed formula.
